d:
Donald Trump isn’t on the ballot. But his last two years in office are. In this explainer, Shubhangi Sharma breaks down how America’s midterm elections work, and why 2026 could reshape Trump’s presidency.
All 435 House seats and 35 Senate seats are up for grabs, along with 36 governorships. Republicans hold the White House and both chambers of Congress, but history is against them: in the last 80 years, the president’s party has gained House seats in a midterm only twice.
